abstract: Carrier-only stimulation ($\Delta f = 0$) is generally considered the most rigorous control for temporal interference (TI) stimulation, assumed to reproduce TI's kilohertz carrier field without its low-frequency beat. We show that this assumption is incorrect: without the frequency difference, the carrier fields interfere coherently, changing the peak strength, power, and direction of the resulting field depending on electrode polarity and montage geometry. Using computational field modeling, we demonstrate that these mismatches can be substantial and widespread. We therefore recommend that TI studies report electrode polarity, model both carrier-field exposures, and choose controls according to their study objectives.
hook: The carrier-only control for temporal interference stimulation changes field strength and direction.
summary: Carrier-only stimulation is often used as the control for temporal interference brain stimulation, on the assumption that it matches the carrier field without the beat. Computational field models show the carrier fields add coherently, so peak strength, power, and direction differ by electrode polarity and montage. The evidence is modeling only, with no experiments in people or animals.
title: Same currents, different field: $\Delta f = 0$ carrier-only stimulation is not temporal interference without the beat
